standard_prerequisites.name: Superstandard tableau T_lambda
standard_prerequisites.statement: T_lambda is the standard Young tableau of shape lambda filled row by row with 1,2,...,N.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both assertions are about T_lambda and its descent set.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent set and conjugate partition
standard_prerequisites.statement: Des(T) is the set of positions i with i+1 in a lower row than i, and lambda' denotes the conjugate partition.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement identifies Des(T_lambda) with [N-1] minus the partial sums of lambda', and the proof argues by columns of the conjugate shape.

core_obligations: Dispose of the first assertion, which is immediate from the row-by-row filling of T_lambda (source lines 573-574).
For the second, take T in Syt(mu) with Des(T) = Des(T_lambda) and T different from T_lambda, and aim for mu' > lambda' (source line 585).

Let i be the first column where T and T_lambda differ; the i-th column of T_lambda carries the entries s+1 to s+lambda'_i with s = lambda'_1 + ... + lambda'_{i-1}, so it suffices that all these entries also occur in the i-th column of T (source line 585).

Assume a minimal such entry x sits in a different column j: if j < i this contradicts the choice of i, and if j > i then x is the minimal entry of that column and therefore x-1 is not a descent of T while it is one of T_lambda (source line 587).

Conclude the contradiction, so all entries of the i-th column of T_lambda lie in the i-th column of T, which forces mu' > lambda' and, in the case mu = lambda, forces T = T_lambda (source lines 575-576 and 587).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the second assertion and set up the first differing column.
Rule out the two possible columns of the minimal misplaced entry.
Conclude the dominance inequality and the uniqueness clause.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:superstandard characterize coefficients` at source lines 570-577: it identifies the descent set of the superstandard tableau T_lambda with [N-1] minus the partial sums of the conjugate partition lambda', and it asserts that any tableau with that descent set has a shape dominating lambda' and is unique when the shape is exactly lambda. The author's proof (source lines 582-588) is a single-page argument that is not bookkeeping: it picks the first column i where a competitor T differs from T_lambda (line 585), reduces the dominance inequality mu' > lambda' to the statement that the i-th column entries of T_lambda all occur in the i-th column of T, and then analyses a minimal misplaced entry x by cases on its column j, using that x is the minimal entry of its column when j > i so that x-1 ceases to be a descent (line 587). The uniqueness clause is read off from the same analysis; the statement records none of the column-wise reasoning.
